issues.description: SQL SELECT list in solution_repository/aufgabe02.sql: The problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 21-24) requires exactly three columns: Freizeitpark.name, Freizeitpark.strasse and Gemeinde.name. The solution (solution_repository/aufgabe02.sql) SELECT returns Freizeitpark.name, Freizeitpark.strasse, Gemeinde.name AND Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel. The template (template_repository/aufgabe02.sql) shows a different starter SELECT (Freizeitpark.name as Park_name, Gemeinde.name as Gemeinde_name). The extra Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel in the solution is not requested by the exercise and can cause automated checks to fail or confuse students about the expected output.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the extra Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel column from solution_repository/aufgabe02.sql so the query returns exactly the requested columns. For example: SELECT Freizeitpark.name, Freizeitpark.strasse, Gemeinde.name FROM Freizeitpark JOIN Gemeinde ON Gemeinde.schluessel = Freizeitpark.gemeindeschluessel;

issues.description: COUNT usage in solution_repository/aufgabe06.sql: The problem (problem_statement.md lines 42-44) asks for the number of Wanderwege that lead to Gemeinden with mehr als 500000 männlichen Einwohnern (i.e., count Wanderwege). The solution (solution_repository/aufgabe06.sql) uses SELECT COUNT(*) on the join between Gemeinde and Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde, which counts join rows (links). If a single Wanderweg links to multiple Gemeinden, COUNT(*) over the join will overcount compared to counting distinct Wanderwege, creating an ambiguity between counting links and counting unique Wanderwege.
issues.suggestedFix: Count distinct Wanderwege rather than join rows. Change the solution to use COUNT(DISTINCT Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde.wanderweg_id) (or COUNT(DISTINCT <appropriate_wanderweg_id_column>) ) with an explicit join, for example: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde.wanderweg_id) FROM Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde JOIN Gemeinde ON Gemeinde.schluessel = Wanderweg_zu_Gemeinde.gemeindeschluessel WHERE Gemeinde.einwohner_m > 500000;

issues.description: COUNT usage in solution_repository/aufgabe08.sql: The problem (problem_statement.md lines 50-52) requests the number of Radwegen that border Gemeinden with PLZ > 96400 (i.e., count Radwege). The solution (solution_repository/aufgabe08.sql) uses SELECT COUNT(*) on the join between Gemeinde and Radweg_zu_Gemeinde, which counts join rows (links). If a single Radweg borders multiple Gemeinden, COUNT(*) will overcount compared to counting distinct Radwege, causing ambiguity between counting links and counting unique Radwege.
issues.suggestedFix: Count distinct Radwege rather than join rows. Change the solution to use COUNT(DISTINCT Radweg_zu_Gemeinde.radweg_id) with an explicit join, for example: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Radweg_zu_Gemeinde.radweg_id) FROM Radweg_zu_Gemeinde JOIN Gemeinde ON Gemeinde.schluessel = Radweg_zu_Gemeinde.gemeindeschluessel WHERE Gemeinde.plz > 96400;
